title: The Black and Tan band, first ragtime band on the West Coast
summary: Foster and the interviewers discuss the Los Angeles Black and Tan band, its trumpeter and players, and Oliver not being first.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Did they use two bands? They had real heavy bands there? Yeah.
But you know what? That wasn't the first ragtime band they had out here.
Oliver was out here too. He wasn't the first.
He wasn't the first. They had a band in Los Angeles. It was the first ragtime band they had on the coast. They had all this work out there.
What's his catch?
He had a trumpet player for a moment called Ernest Corkette. He called himself Ernest Johnson, the black and tan band. Isn't he? Isn't he?
Isn't he? I think he's up in San Bernardino. He's dead, I think, of course. Is he dead now?
I don't understand.
All the black and tans are dead now. No, no, Leon White is living. Leon Hussard. Paul Howard is the president.
He's in the union there. Yeah.
Half-Sons.
Howard is the president. He's in the union there. Yeah. How old is that? No, Howard is dead.
He's a Toronto player.
Had a barber shot at you?
Jack, Jackson.
He wrote that number they called Jack the Bear, you remember? Who did?
Jackson.

He played piano, then later he turned on to play Tujo. Jackson, yeah. He had a big everything. You remember? Who did? Jackson. He played piano, then later he turned on to play Tujo. Jackson, yeah. He had a big everything. You remember? He was a big guy. He was a big guy. He was a big guy.
Buster, I think, played with him for a while. And Dick Thompson. Buster Buster. No, no.

Not that band. Buster Buster? No. Not the time I know. See, this band was way back then, man, before. Way back then. Way back then. Years ago, Korns had a book out, and that was the only Negro band picture was ever advertising anything that had black and tan band in the advertising, in Korns Music Book. Do you remember that? Yeah. And they had their uniforms, man, so different. Yeah.
I'd like to say that, that came out.
